description: Ace of Cards is a team of passionate and innovative young minds driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared love for science and technology. We bring together diverse skills and perspectives to solve problems, explore new possibilities, and turn ideas into meaningful solutions.
summary: The team developed an interactive 3d space game simulation that allows you to explore and operate missions that makes space education more engaging, accessible, and educational. The game allows players to navigate and experience remote missions through three primary missions: conducting astronomical observations of Jupiter using a simulated Hubble Space Telescope, piloting a robotic rover across the Martian landscape to explore geological formations and collect scientific samples, and help navigate astronauts around the ISS for maintenance. The Mars mission also introduces a simulated emergency scenario that makes players locate while also assisting a stranded rover that experiences power reduction following a dust storm. Unlike ordinary space games that uses a mouse or keyboard, our game uses something that a lot of people already have, your smartphones. Players can connect their smartphones to a PC and use them as dedicated mission controllers. Alongside this is an AI commander that helps players have a smooth and clear experience. By integrating interactive gameplay, immersive 3D environments, and scientifically grounded NASA information, MISSION: ORION addresses the challenge of presenting complex space science concepts in an engaging and understandable way. The project promotes interactive learning, curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving while developing a deeper appreciation of space exploration, planetary science, and technological innovation.
details:
What exactly does it do?
MISSION: ORION is an interactive 3D space exploration and mission simulation game that allows users to experience different space missions. It features two main missions: observing Jupiter using a simulated Hubble Space Telescope, exploring the surface of Mars using a robotic rover, and help navigate astronauts around the ISS for maintenance. Through these activities, users can learn about space exploration while completing mission tasks.


How does it work?
The game allows users to take part in three different missions. In the first mission, users operate a simulated Hubble Space Telescope to observe Jupiter, including its Great Red Spot and Galilean moons. In the second mission, users control a Mars rover to explore the Martian surface, examine geological formations, and collect scientific samples. In the third mission, the player helps navigate an astronaut around the International Space Station for maintenance viewing through the astronaut's headcam simulating how astronauts communicate with ground control. The Mars mission also includes an emergency situation where users must assist a stranded rover with low power after a dust storm. A smartphone can be used as a remote controller for the telescope and rover, while an AI Commander provides mission instructions and guidance.


What benefits does it have?
MISSION: ORION makes learning about space exploration more interactive and engaging. It helps users understand astronomy, planetary science, and the role of technology in space missions. By completing different tasks, users can also develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. The project provides an enjoyable way to learn about space while encouraging interest in science and technology.

What is the intended impact of the project?
The goal of MISSION: ORION is to make space science more accessible and interesting through an interactive learning experience. It aims to help users better understand how space missions work and the challenges faced by astronauts, scientists, and robotic explorers. The project also hopes to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage more learners to take an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).


What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, HTML and CSS.

Software and Libraries:

  • Three.js – 3D game rendering
  • Vite and Node.js – development and local server
  • WebSockets – smartphone controller connection
  • Blender – 3D modeling
  • glTF-Transform and meshoptimizer – 3D model optimization
  • geotiff and sharp – terrain and texture processing
  • Playwright – automated testing
  • ElevenLabs – AI voice and sound effects
  • VS Code, Git and GitHub – development and version control
  • Claude Code – AI coding assistance

Data Sources: NASA and USGS datasets, including HiRISE terrain data, Jupiter maps, Earth imagery, star maps, and NASA 3D models of the ISS, Perseverance and Hubble.

Hardware: Windows 11 PC for development and gameplay, and a smartphone as an optional wireless controller. The game runs offline in a web browser without specialized hardware.


How is your project creative?
MISSION: ORION combines 3D space environments, interactive missions, and realistic space exploration activities in one game. It allows users to experience both astronomical observation and robotic exploration. The smartphone-as-controller feature adds another level of interaction, while the AI Commander provides instructions and explanations throughout the missions. These features create a more engaging way to learn about space.


What factors did your team consider?
The team considered factors such as educational value, user experience, ease of control, and engagement. The missions were designed to help users understand space science through activities that involve observation, exploration, and problem-solving. The team also considered the importance of clear mission instructions, interactive controls, and an AI Commander that guides users throughout the experience. These factors help make MISSION: ORION both educational and enjoyable.
